## 2. Symptom (observable) + reproducibility profile
- **DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION** within **5–10 s of booting Windows** when the platform attempts **PkgC6/PkgC10**
  with **UFS as primary storage** and the **Intel GFx driver installed** `[confirmed, Comment 1666658421]`.
- **Three distinct failure signatures** `[confirmed, Comment 1666658421 (msure)]`:
  1. **BSOD-only** — hits BSOD as soon as Windows boots; UFS registers **not accessible** except IOSF2OCP PCI
     config space; StatusScope dump **corrupted**; memory dump stuck at **0%**. Bugchecks seen:
     **`DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION`, `CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT`, `MACHINE_CHECK_EXCEPTION`, `WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR`**.
  2. **CAT-error-only** — UFS registers accessible, UFS IP fully active; StatusScope dump capturable and shows a
     **pending transaction to UFS**; app SW accessing **`IS_`** + **`UTRLDBR`**; `IS_` = **SBFES + HCFES**;
     `HCS` has **`UICCMDRDY`/`UTRLRDY`/`UTMRLRDY` cleared** (host controller not ready). MCA: **THREE_STRIKE core
     hung + ROB TIMEOUT**.
  3. **Both** CAT error **and** BSOD after boot.
- **At the recovery screen** `[confirmed, Comment 1566152567]`: **UFS controller in D3 + power-gated; UFS M-PHY
  up + NOT power-gated.** UFS link enters/exits **H8 with data transfer, 1000 cycles pass at UEFI shell** →
  UFS is functionally clean in isolation.
- **Reproducibility gates (GFx × PkgC matrix, Comment 1566165755):**

  | GFx driver | PkgC state | OS boot | BSOD |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Inbox | Enabled | Pass | not observed |
  | Inbox | Disabled | Pass | not observed |
  | **Intel** | **Enabled** | **Fail** | **BSOD <10 s** |
  | Intel | Disabled | Pass | not observed |
  | **Intel** | **Limited to C6** | **Fail** | **BSOD <10 s** |
  | Intel | Limited to C0 | Pass | not observed |

- **Other gates:** UFS=primary required (NVMe-primary + UFS-secondary → **no repro**, Comment 1666622654 #4);
  bare wim image (no PKGC attempted) → no repro; **VTd disabled → still repros** (Comment 1666622654 #5);
  fails **PkgC6.1/C10.1** but **not** PkgC6.2/10.2/10.3 (`sysdbg_notes4`, ggohjong); **works on ChromeOS**
  (UFS 3.1 reaches PKGC10, Comment 1666670795). **LNL and NVL report the same signature** (forum_notes WW19.1).

## 3. Initial triage — first discriminators
- **Rule-in (it IS this / P1):** UFS-primary + **PkgC6 or deeper** + **Intel GFx driver** → DPC/CLOCK watchdog
  within 10 s; `IS_` **SBFES+HCFES**; **THREE_STRIKE on CORE2**; StatusScope shows **non-posted UFS txn stuck,
  PSF completion tracker not drained PSF0.PSF4→PSF4.UFS** (§5a). This is the P1 fabric-timeout fingerprint.
- **Rule-out (it is NOT this) — exact conditions:**
  - Repro with **PkgC limited to C0 / PKGC disabled**? **NO** → not this (power-state entry is the trigger).
  - Repro with **Inbox GFx** (no Intel GFx)? **NO** → the **Intel GFx driver is a gate** (it is what makes the
    platform actually attempt deep PkgC residency).
  - Repro with **NVMe as primary**? **NO** → UFS-primary-specific.
  - UFS HW broken? **NO** — UFS passes **1000 H8 enter/exit cycles at UEFI shell**; clean on ChromeOS.
- **Nearest look-alike = the thing it IS:** `16027585017` (P1). Deciding tell that they're the **same**: both
  show **SBFES+HCFES + THREE_STRIKE CORE2 + PSF4→UFS stuck + PkgC-gated + GFx-gated + NVMe-passes**, and the
  **axon StatusScope record `019633cb` is linked to BOTH sightings**. (Contrast the *other* WCL UFS classes:
  NOT the boot fuse-pull CDC race `16029205689` (P2); NOT the HLK endpoint-reset soft-hang `16029554884`.)

## 4. Reproduction recipe (config, images, IFWI, knobs, operating point)
- **Boards:** WCL **PW01 RVP** (DDR5) and **ERB** (LP5); **M.2 UFS** — both **discrete M.2** and **combo port**
  repro; FAB1 and FAB3 M.2 UFS both repro (Comment 1666634359). UFS channel trace length within spec.
- **IFWI:** `WCL_PR04_A0A0-…_UFS_2025WW11.1.01_TestBios…` (RVP1) / `WCL_PR02_A0A0-…_UFS_2025WW10.1.01` (ERB).
- **BKC:** `WCL-U-2024-CONS-25.14.6.61` WIM (`26100.3323`). **GFx driver:** `gfx-driver-ci-…-ptl-139-…-wcl`
  (also Intel GFx `6682`).
- **Knob:** BIOS → Intel Advanced Menu → Power & Performance → **Package C states → Enable** (PkgC6+).
- **Expect:** boot Windows with Intel GFx + PkgC6/C10 → **DPC_WATCHDOG / CAT error within 5–10 s**.
- **Mitigation to avoid repro:** limit PkgC to C0 / disable PKGC; or NVMe-primary; or bare wim (no PKGC). The
  **durable fix is P1's BIOS 650 µs UFS-LTR workaround** (§8 / see 16027585017).

## 6. Debug flow (diagnostic narrowing)
1. **Is UFS HW broken?** No — 1000× H8 enter/exit pass at UEFI shell; clean on ChromeOS → **functional UFS is
   fine**; the failure needs the Windows PKGC flow.
2. **Is it the GFx HW/driver directly?** No direct GFx↔UFS HW path (msure, Comment 1666609435). The **Intel GFx
   driver is a *gate*** — it's what lets the platform actually attempt deep PkgC residency (RC6 entry/exit);
   Inbox GFx / GFx-disabled never arms the failing window (§2 matrix).
3. **Where does it hang?** StatusScope (§5a): a **non-posted UFS read is stuck**, PSF completion tracker not
   drained **PSF0.PSF4→PSF4.UFS** → **CCF stuck** → a **LOCK flow has quiesced the cores (`Stop_Core` /
   `Stop_Core_Cmp`)** and cannot complete because it waits behind the stuck UFS txn → **uncore hang** →
   THREE_STRIKE CORE2 → **`storufs!UfsResetBus`** can't finish in time → **DPC_WATCHDOG**.
4. **Why only PkgC6+?** Issue is in the **memory path** relevance of PkgC (ggohjong, `sysdbg_notes4`): fails
   **PkgC6.1/C10.1**, not 6.2/10.2/10.3 → a specific deep-state resource/latency window. This is the **OCP
   fabric-timeout-waiting-for-system-resource** mechanism root-caused on **P1**.
5. **Scope:** same signature on **LNL and NVL** → not a one-off WCL board defect; a shared fabric/LTR design gap.

## 7. Root cause (precise mechanism + class)
- **Root cause `[via-P1, 16027585017]`:** **OCP (Sonics) fabric timeout waiting for a system resource** during
  deep PkgC — **UFS 3.1 does not request an LTR to the PMC**, so when a UFS non-posted transaction needs
  core/ring/memory resources that were power-managed away on PkgC6+ entry, the fabric times out → `IS_`
  **SBFES/HCFES** → host controller stops. **Class: design-rtl** (missing LTR reporting), surfaced by the
  power-management interaction. The **BIOS 650 µs UFS-LTR workaround** resolves it (see P1 §8).
- **This sighting's added mechanism detail (StatusScope, §5a):** the stuck UFS non-posted read does not just
  hang the UFS path — it **blocks an in-flight LOCK/atomic flow that had already quiesced the cores**
  (`cNCU/sNCU` lock FSM in `Stop_Core` → `Stop_Core_Cmp` → `LKFSM_STOP_REQ_1_CNCU`). Because the lock cannot
  retire until the UFS data returns, the **cores never resume** → **uncore hang** → THREE_STRIKE CORE2 and the
  DPC/CLOCK watchdogs. This is the concrete chain from "one stuck UFS read" to "whole-SoC hang," and is the
  piece P1's record does not yet spell out.
- **Why GFx matters:** `[inferred]` the Intel GFx driver is the component that drives the platform into the
  deep PkgC residency (RC6 entry/exit) where the LTR-less UFS transaction can collide with resource removal;
  without it the deep window is never entered (§2 matrix). Not a GFx HW defect.

### 7b. Fingerprint registers (high level)
- **`IS_` SBFES (bit 17) + HCFES (bit 16)** — fatal, non-recoverable UFSHCI error-status; set at the hang →
  HC stops, OS `IS_` read wedges → BSOD/MCA/>20 s reset. (Full decode → `reference/ufs-glossary.md`.)
- **`HCS` `UICCMDRDY`/`UTRLRDY`/`UTMRLRDY` cleared** — HC not ready; it went bad before SW rang `UTRLDBR`.
- **StatusScope FSM fingerprint** — `cNCU_IDI_Bridge … Stop_Core_Cmp` + `sNCU … LKFSM_STOP_REQ_1_CNCU` +
  `PSF0.PSF4→PSF4.UFS` tracker ≠ 0 = the decisive uncore-lock-hang-behind-stuck-UFS signature.

## 8. Fix & verification (or workaround + status)
- **This sighting:** **no independent fix** — `rejected / merged` into P1, and **rejected from IVE** (UFS clean
  on ChromeOS; debug moved to Sergey/MTC on the Windows side). Experiments tried here and their results feed P1.
- **Durable fix `[via-P1, 16027585017]`:** report **UFS LTR ≈ 650 µs** (BIOS), later refined to ignore/disqualify
  UFS LTR on UFS-D3/S0ix entry and re-qualify on D0/exit — restores deep S0ix residency while preventing the
  fabric timeout. IP/PCH fix was **rejected/wont_fix** (ticket 16027667860); fix pushed to **BIOS**
  (14025261732). 100-cycle regression passed on P1. **Not re-validated on this sighting (merged).**
- **Dead-end experiments recorded here** (so they are not re-run): BIOS "disable OCP fabric-timeout" experiment;
  `soc.pmc.mmr.ltr_ign` (no luck); UFS Vcc 2.5 V/1.2 V droop probe (Sergey hypothesis, Comment 22611068479 —
  PTL had a droop once, but UFS here is clean at shell); Auto-Hibernate disable via `storufs.inf` FeatureFlags
  (`0x08000011`) — **not possible**, MSFT locks boot-phase drivers (Comments 1666607603, 1666665830).

## 9. Retrospective (avoidable? prevention? detection gap?)
- **Dead-ends / false leads (do not rechase):**
  - **"GFx HW directly corrupts UFS"** — no silicon GFx↔UFS path; GFx driver is only the **PkgC-residency enabler**.
  - **UFS Vcc droop** (PTL prior art) — probed; UFS is clean at UEFI shell (1000 H8 cycles) → not a supply droop.
  - **Auto-Hibernate / `storufs.inf` FeatureFlags tweak** — MSFT-locked; cannot modify; and Sergey notes AH only
    affects HC↔flash, not the PCIe/root-complex WHEA errors seen here.
  - **VTd** — disabling VTd still repros → not an IOMMU issue.
- **Detection gap:** needs **Win + UFS-primary + Intel-GFx + PkgC6+** together; bare-wim / Inbox-GFx / PKGC0 all
  mask it → put this exact concurrency in the validation matrix (same lesson as P1).
- **Prevention:** validate **LTR-to-PMC reporting** for any PkgC-boot-device IP before enabling deep PkgC with
  it as primary storage (the P1 prevention).

## 12. Debug story
This one looks scary on the surface and is actually a **duplicate of a bug we already understand** (P1,
`16027585017`) — the system blue-screens with `DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION` within ten seconds of booting Windows,
but only in a very specific recipe: **UFS as the primary drive, the Intel graphics driver installed, and the
BIOS allowed to enter deep package-sleep (PkgC6 or deeper).** Take any one of those away — limit the package
C-state to C0, use the inbox graphics driver, or boot from NVMe — and it never happens. The UFS chip itself is
fine: at the UEFI shell it sails through a thousand sleep/wake (H8) cycles, and the identical hardware runs
clean on ChromeOS.

The graphics driver is a red herring in the usual sense — there is no secret wire between the GFx and UFS
hardware. What the GFx driver actually does is let the platform reach the **deep package-sleep residency**;
that's the real trigger. Once there, a single UFS disk read goes out onto the on-die fabric and **never comes
back** — the tooling (StatusScope, pulled straight from the failure database) shows the UFS transaction stuck,
the PSF fabric completion tracker between PSF0/PSF4 and UFS never draining, and the request piling up at the
CCF. The reason a *single* stuck read takes down the whole machine is the part this sighting adds to the story:
right at that moment an **atomic "lock" operation was in flight that had already paused all the cores**
(`Stop_Core`), and that lock can't finish until the UFS read returns. It never returns — so the cores never
un-pause, the uncore hangs, a core trips its **THREE-STRIKE** timeout, and Windows' watchdog fires the BSOD.
(You can even watch the collateral: an interrupt left un-acknowledged, twelve power-domains caught mid
power-state transition.)

*Why* the UFS read gets stuck is the root cause that lives on the P1 record: on WCL, **UFS never tells the power
manager how quickly it needs to be serviced (it doesn't report an LTR)**, so when the platform drops into deep
package-sleep and powers resources down, a UFS transaction that needs them can't get them in time and the fabric
times out — lighting up the UFS controller's fatal error bits (`SBFES`/`HCFES`). The durable fix, also on P1,
is a BIOS change that reports a **~650 µs UFS latency requirement** so the power manager keeps UFS serviceable.
This particular sighting was **merged into P1 and rejected from the IVE side** (UFS is clean in isolation and on
ChromeOS, so the debug moved to Microsoft's Windows storage team) — its lasting value is the failure-database
capture that pins the exact "stuck-UFS-read → stalled lock → uncore hang" chain, and the clean experiment matrix
proving the GFx-driver-plus-deep-PkgC trigger. The same signature was later seen on **LNL and NVL**, confirming
it's a shared design gap, not a one-off board.
